extracted.intended_audience: scholars, editors, and informed readers of Addison & Steele; textual editors of early-18th-century works
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and editorial principles for producing a scholarly, historically-faithful edition of The Spectator (Addison & Steele), including how to handle variants, punctuation, spelling, mottos, notes, and typographic conventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reprint the text as its authors left it
rubrics_metrics.description: This volume reprints for the first time in the present century the text of the 'Spectator' as its authors left it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid wilful alteration of the text; do not modernize or 'correct' Addison's grammar or style. Preserve original readings rather than adopting corruptions or editorial 'improvements' introduced by earlier editors (Bisset, Chalmers, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mark sentences added in reprint with square brackets
rubrics_metrics.description: Sentences added in the reprint are placed between square brackets [ ].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Added material is bracketed without any appended note. Bracketing signals editorial insertions distinct from authors' original revised text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Show omissions/alterations by bracketing revised version and footnoting original
rubrics_metrics.description: Sentences omitted, or words altered, are shown by bracketing the revised version, and giving the text as it stood in the original daily issue within corresponding brackets as a foot-note.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This practice lets the reader see both the authors' revised (permanent) text and the original daily-issue wording; if bracketed insertions are omitted and corresponding footnotes substituted the text becomes that of the original daily numbers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve original spelling and authors' punctuation methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Reproduce original spelling and the authors' own methods of punctuating and use of capitals to retain the harmony of their style.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not modernize spellings or punctuation except where necessary for sense; aim to show 'not only what Steele and Addison wrote, but how they spelt' and how they used capitals for emphasis. Only very minor differences in Queen Anne's spelling that do not obscure sense may be tolerated, but the preference is faithful reproduction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow original folio typographic conventions (italics, punctuation rows, etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: The original folio numbers have been followed also in the use of italics [_shown between underscored thus_] and other little details of the disposition of the type; for example, in the reproduction of those rows of single inverted commas which distinguish certain parts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reproduce typographic features (italics, inverted commas, placement of mottos) as in the original folio issues. If specific formatting cannot be reproduced in a medium (e.g., plain-text file), note the omission to the reader.

rubrics_metrics.name: Place translations of mottos and Latin quotations in an Appendix
rubrics_metrics.description: The translation of the mottos and Latin quotations, which Steele and Addison deliberately abstained from giving, are here placed in a body at the end, for those who want them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep the original practice of withholding translations from the running text; provide translations separately in an appendix to avoid impeding or confusing the main text and to respect the authors' banter about mottos.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include an Appendix of advertisements from the original numbers
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a short Appendix also of advertisements taken from the original number of the 'Spectator', and a few others, where they seem to illustrate some point in the text, will be found among the notes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select advertisements that illuminate historical context or textual points and place them in an appendix rather than interrupting the main essays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Add notes to assist acquaintance with writers and allusions
rubrics_metrics.description: In the large number of notes here added to a revision of those bequeathed to us by Percy and Calder, the object has been to give information which may contribute to some nearer acquaintance with the writers of the book, and enjoyment of allusions to past manners and events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use notes to explain personal allusions, historical references, and points of authorship; incorporate reliable oral and documentary traditions (as Percy and Calder did) while distinguishing original attributions (e.g., mark Percy’s notes with 'P.' and Calder’s as 'Annotator').

rubrics_metrics.name: Collate multiple source-issues to show amount and character of revision
rubrics_metrics.description: The papers as they first appeared in the daily issue ... have been closely compared with the first issue in guinea octavos, for which they were revised, and with the last edition that appeared before the death of Steele. The original text is here given precisely as it was left after revision by its authors; and there is shown at the same time the amount and character of the revision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare daily numbers, early octavo reprints, and later editions to identify authorial revisions versus compositor/printing corruptions; present both the stable (revised) text and the variant/daily-issue readings where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retain and augment a general index for reference
rubrics_metrics.description: From the 'General Index to the Spectators, &c.,' published as a separate volume in 1760, there has been taken what was serviceable, and additions have been made to it with a desire to secure for this edition ... the advantages of being handy for reference as well as true to the real text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a comprehensive and usable index (built on older indexes but augmented) so the edition serves both scholarly reference and faithful textual presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document editorial provenance of notes and corrections
rubrics_metrics.description: Percy's notes have a P. attached to them, and Dr. Calder's are signed 'Annotator.' Percy actually edited two volumes ... their notes are those of which the substance has run through all subsequent editions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly label editorial contributions and trace which historical editor supplied particular notes or emendations so readers can judge provenance and reliability; avoid unnoted emendations that obscure history of editorial decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid perpetuating misprints and deliberate modernization introduced by earlier editors
rubrics_metrics.description: Since that time not only have misprints been preserved and multiplied, but punctuation has been deliberately modernized, to the destruction of the freshness of the original style, and editors of another 'understanding age' have also taken upon themselves by many a little touch to correct Addison's style or grammar.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resist earlier editors' tendencies to 'correct' perceived faults of style or grammar; prefer to restore original readings and punctuation to preserve author's voice and historical flavor.
